primitives.name: Temper Correlation Table
primitives.verbatim_quote: 231 On comparing the entries, especially the summaries in the lower lines of the Table, it does not seem that the characters of near relatives are treated much more tenderly than those of the more remote.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes unbiased recording of temperaments across familial distances; no systematic emotional bias in compilation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No known breakdown; assumes consistent data quality across all family relationships.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian network where nodes represent temperaments and edges represent conditional independence given familial distance.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation from expected temperament similarity in direct versus indirect line records

primitives.name: Compilers Bias Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is little indication of the compilers having been biased by affection, respect, or fear.
primitives.assumptions: Compilers treat all relatives equally regardless of proximity; no preferential recording based on sentiment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bias emerges if compilations systematically omit negative traits in closer relatives.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction intervals for temperament records adjusted for potential social desirability bias.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of missing temperament data points relative to expected rates

primitives.name: Omission Ignorance Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: More cases of a record being left blank when a bad temper ought to have been recorded, would probably occur in the direct line, but I do not see how this could be tested.
primitives.assumptions: Omissions are random and independent of actual temperament; compilators lack complete knowledge of all relatives.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Omission rate becomes problematic when linked to specific temperamental outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Expectation-Maximization algorithm to estimate missing temperament data under ignorability assumptions.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of incomplete records vs. known informant reliability metrics
